winners.title: The Medal His Father Was Asked to Present
winners.premise: A son sells his father's bravery medal with a promise that the father will present it to the buyer and call him a hero.
winners.conflict: A father who agreed to sell an important possession must refuse his son's attempt to sell the meaning of his service along with it.
winners.twist: The buyer was told the father had personally chosen him for an honorary presentation and does not know the father needs the sale money.
winners.hook: A son sold his father's bravery medal with a promise the buyer would be called a hero. His father hadn't agreed to give that speech.
winners.narration: Arthur had agreed to sell the medal because he needed the money. When his son handed him a speech before the meeting, he found instructions to praise the buyer's courage and make a formal presentation. Arthur asked when he'd agreed to that. His son, Dean, said the ceremony was what made the sale worth enough to help. Arthur said owning the medal wouldn't give somebody his history. Dean told him not to embarrass the man who was paying. The buyer, Peter, arrived carrying a display case. He thanked Arthur for choosing him, saying Dean had described it as a personal honor. Arthur asked whether Peter knew the medal was being sold. Peter looked at Dean. Dean said everyone was getting something they wanted and asked Arthur to read the speech before making it awkward. Arthur put the paper down. He said he would tell Peter what the medal meant, but wouldn't pretend Peter had earned it. Peter closed the display case and asked to hear the real story. Dean reminded his father that they still needed the money. Arthur asked Peter directly whether he wanted to buy the object with its history told honestly. Peter said yes. Arthur handed him the medal himself. There was no announcement about a new hero. Peter asked whose name should go beside it in the case. The medal changed hands. The story kept its real name.
winners.description: Arthur agrees to sell his medal, then discovers his son has promised a presentation he never approved.
winners.payoff: The story kept its real name.
winners.like_cta: LIKE IF HONOR IS NOT FOR SALE
tags: veteran asked to honor medal buyer

winners.title: The Car Outside Her Father's Award Photo
winners.premise: A father wins recognition for housing the daughter he evicted and asks her to hide the car she has been sleeping in before a publicity photograph.
winners.conflict: A daughter must choose whether to help her father stage generosity in exchange for another promise of support.
winners.twist: The key he gives her is only a prop for the photograph, and he still refuses to let her move back in.
winners.hook: A father won a housing award for a daughter he'd evicted. He asked her to move the car she'd been sleeping in out of the photograph.
winners.narration: Jade parked outside the house after her father said he wanted to help her. Instead of asking about a room, he handed her a key and told her to stand by the front door. The photographer had been told he'd kept his daughter safely housed through a difficult year. Jade asked whether the key meant she could come home. Her father, Neil, said they could discuss that after the pictures. Then he noticed the blanket on her back seat and asked her to park farther down the road. Neil said people would get the wrong idea. She said it would be the first accurate part of the photograph. He reminded her that the award might bring opportunities to help her with a rental deposit. The photographer lowered the camera and asked whether Jade actually lived there. Neil said she had chosen to leave. Jade asked him to open the door and show them the room he was keeping for her. He told her not to start that conversation in front of a stranger. She put the key back in his hand. She said she wasn't going to turn another promise into proof that he'd already helped. Neil asked whether she wanted to ruin something good for the family. Jade picked up her own keys. She moved the car only after the camera was packed away. This time, she was leaving, not hiding.
winners.description: Jade arrives hoping her father will offer help and finds he needs her for a photograph of help he never gave.
winners.like_cta: LIKE IF THE PHOTO SHOULD BE TRUE
tags: father wins award for housing evicted daughter
father offers key as photo prop

winners.title: The Dress at Her Funeral Suit Fitting
winners.premise: A daughter secretly pays a tailor to replace her mother's chosen funeral suit with a dress while her mother is still alive to attend the fitting.
winners.conflict: An older woman must defend her own choice while her daughter treats future grief as permission to decide how she will be remembered.
winners.twist: The daughter has removed the pockets her mother specifically requested, exposing how little the replacement reflects the woman who will wear it.
winners.hook: A woman found her funeral suit had been turned into a dress. Her daughter had paid for the change, even though her mother was still alive to choose.
winners.narration: Dora asked the tailor where the jacket and trousers were. He said her daughter had called with new instructions and covered the cost. Elise held the dress against her mother and said it would look softer in the photographs. Dora asked where the pockets had gone. Elise said she wouldn't need pockets then. Dora told her she had asked for somewhere to put the peppermints she always carried. The tailor put down his pins. Elise said she was trying to make a difficult thing easier and asked her mother to try it on before rejecting it. Dora said the difficult part was standing in the room while people discussed her as if she had already left it. Elise started crying and said everyone would remember the last thing they saw her wearing. Dora asked whether her daughter remembered her in a dress or in the suits she'd worn for years. Elise looked at the garment in her hands. Dora said she wasn't asking her to stop being sad, but to stop using that sadness to change the order. The tailor asked Dora what she wanted him to make. She repeated her choice, including the pockets. Elise asked whether she could still come to the next fitting. Dora said yes, and asked her to bring the peppermints. There were things they could still choose together. Her mother was still there to ask.
winners.description: Dora arrives for a fitting and learns that her daughter has replaced her chosen clothes with a version meant for everyone else's memories.
winners.payoff: Her mother was still there to ask.
tags: woman finds dress at tailor fitting
mother wants funeral suit with pockets
older woman chooses her own clothes

winners.title: The Cleaner in Their Custody Argument
winners.premise: A divorcing couple argues over which household will get their cleaner without asking whether she wants to keep working for either of them.
winners.conflict: A cleaner must establish that her job and family life cannot be divided as part of her employers' marriage.
winners.twist: She has already accepted another job so she can spend afternoons with her own daughter, whose needs neither employer has considered.
winners.hook: A divorcing couple argued over who would get custody of their cleaner. She was standing beside them with her resignation letter.
winners.narration: Rosa had come to collect her things when Helen asked whether she preferred alternate weeks or fixed days. Helen's husband, Mark, said Rosa should stay with him because he had hired her first. Rosa put the envelope on the kitchen table. Helen moved it aside and said they could solve the schedule before dealing with paperwork. Rosa explained that it was her notice. Mark asked whether Helen had offered her more money. Helen said she would match it. Rosa said neither had asked whether she wanted another offer. She had accepted a school kitchen job and would finish in time to collect her daughter. Mark said she could do mornings at his house and afternoons at Helen's instead. Rosa asked when she was supposed to collect her child. Helen told him not to be unreasonable, then asked Rosa to stay through the move because she was practically family. Rosa said she had a family of her own. Helen asked who would help sort the linen if she left now. Mark said that should be Helen's responsibility because she was keeping the cupboard. Rosa picked up her coat. She pointed to the notice and told them her last working date was written inside. They began arguing about the cupboard again. Rosa left them to it and walked to the school. The only child she was collecting that afternoon was her own.
winners.description: Rosa's employers try to divide her working life during their divorce, while she has already made plans for her own family.
winners.payoff: The only child she was collecting that afternoon was her own.
winners.like_cta: LIKE IF ROSA CHOOSES HER OWN LIFE
tags: employers treat cleaner as family property
